newsitem.title: USA: Calif. tax revenues top budget projections - report.
newsitem.headline: Calif. tax revenues top budget projections - report.

text.p: California general fund revenues during the first three months of the fiscal year exceeded the budget forecast, the state's Legislative Analyst said in a report Friday.
Revenues were up $233 million in September, bringing cumulative receipts for the first three months of the fiscal year to $415 million above the budget forecast.
About $130 million of the increase was due to unusually large estate tax payments in September. These payments represented a one-time gain to the general fund.

About $79 million of the gain was due to general fund receipts of trial court revenues that the budget had assumed would be allocated to a trust fund beginning in 1996-1997. However, the implementation legislation was not approved and the revenues continued to be deposited in the general fund.
Assuming trial court revenues are appropriated to local trial courts, the gain will be offset by higher expenditures in the coming months, the Legislative Analyst said.
"Thus, there probably will be no net gain to the general fund's 'bottom line,'" the report said, referring to trial court revenues.
The remainder of the $415 million gain was consistent with the generally positive economic trends in California, the Legislative Analyst said.
The report noted, however, that quarterly prepayments on 1996 corporate earnings came in lower than expected, a possible sign of a slowdown in taxable corporate profits.

"The weakeness is somewhat puzzling in light of the positive industry reports on corporation earnings for the third quarter of 1996, and the continuing economic growth in California during this period," the Legislative Analyst said.
